headline: Would have canceled a Washington, D.C. law that changed police rules, including neck restraint bans, body camera procedures, and access to discipline records.
what_it_does: This resolution would have blocked a D.C. Council law called the Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act of 2022. That D.C. law bans certain neck restraints by police, adds procedures for body-worn cameras, and expands access to police disciplinary records. The President vetoed the resolution, and the House failed to override the veto, so the D.C. law was not canceled.

who_it_affects.how: They would no longer have been covered by the D.C. law's limits on neck restraints and its added body camera procedures.

who_it_affects.group: People living in or visiting Washington, D.C.
who_it_affects.how: They would have lost the expanded access to police disciplinary records and other policing rules set by the D.C. law.

who_it_affects.group: The D.C. Council and local government
who_it_affects.how: A policing law the Council passed would have been overturned by Congress.
